stem.en: The trail of data we leave behind while using the Internet is called:

explanation.en: Every online activity — posts, searches, visits — leaves a record that is called a digital footprint.

stem.en: Which of these is an example of a PASSIVE digital footprint?

options.en: A comment you post on a video
An email you send to your teacher
The websites you visited, recorded by your browser and the sites through cookies
An online form you fill in

explanation.en: Passive footprints are collected without our knowing action, like browsing history, IP address and cookies. Posting, emailing and filling forms are active footprints.

stem.en: Which statement about digital footprints is TRUE?

options.en: Digital footprints are stored only on your own device
Digital footprints can be used to trace a user, their location and habits
Only social media posts create digital footprints
Deleting a post from your profile always removes every copy from the Internet

explanation.en: Footprints are stored on servers and can be copied, so deleting a post may not remove all copies; they can be used to trace users.

solution.en: Footprints are stored on servers and can be copied, so deleting a post may not remove all copies; they can be used to trace users.

stem.en: A student wants to keep her digital footprint small. Which habit helps MOST?

options.en: Posting her location with every photo
Thinking before posting and sharing only what is necessary
Using the same password on all sites

explanation.en: Sharing only what is needed and thinking before posting reduces the trail of personal data.

stem.en: A person who uses the Internet and digital technology responsibly as a member of the online community is called a:

explanation.en: Netizen = net + citizen: a responsible member of the digital society.

stem.en: Which of these is good communication etiquette when sending an email?

options.en: Forwarding it to everyone in your contact list
Typing the whole message in CAPITAL LETTERS
Being precise and avoiding large attachments unless necessary

explanation.en: Be precise: respect the reader's time and data limits. All capitals reads as shouting.

stem.en: Someone posts deliberately provocative comments to upset people on a forum. The netiquette advice is:

options.en: Don't feed the troll — ignore and report
Copy the comments to other forums

explanation.en: Trolls want attention; ignoring and reporting them is the responsible response.

stem.en: Which of these violates the "be respectful" netiquette?

options.en: Crediting the source of an image
Using polite language in a group chat
Sharing a classmate's photo without permission

explanation.en: Respecting privacy means not sharing others' photos or details without consent.

solution.en: Respecting privacy means not sharing others' photos or details without consent.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Typing a message entirely in capital letters is considered bad netiquette.
Reason (R): On the Internet, text in all capital letters is generally read as shouting.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true and R explains A.

stem.en: Which IPR protects an original invention, giving the inventor exclusive rights for a limited period (usually 20 years)?

explanation.en: A patent is granted for inventions; the protection is usually for 20 years, after which the invention is public.

stem.en: Presenting someone else's work or idea as your own without giving credit is called:

explanation.en: Plagiarism is using another person's work without acknowledgement; it is a violation of IPR ethics.

stem.en: Which licence is mainly designed to give public access to SOFTWARE, so that it can be used, studied, modified and shared?

explanation.en: GPL is a widely used free software licence. Creative Commons is used mainly for creative works like text, images, music and websites.

solution.en: GPL is a widely used free software licence.
Creative Commons is used mainly for creative works like text, images, music and websites.

stem.en: A company's logo and brand name are protected by:

explanation.en: A trademark protects a visual symbol, word, name or design that identifies a brand.

stem.en:
A student downloads a copyrighted song, edits it slightly and uploads it as her own on a video platform. Which statements are correct?
(i) It is copyright infringement.
(ii) It is legal because she edited the song.
(iii) She should take permission or use a song with a suitable licence.

explanation.en: Using copyrighted work without permission is infringement even if it is edited; she should obtain permission or use openly licensed music.

stem.en: Which licence fits the SONG best?

explanation.en: Creative Commons licences are designed for creative works and allow conditions like attribution (BY) and non-commercial (NC).

passage.en: A college music club records an original song and wants others to share it freely, but only with credit to the club and not for commercial use. The club's app developer also writes code for the club website and wants anyone to be able to use, modify and redistribute the code, as long as their changes are also shared under the same terms.

stem.en: Which licence fits the website CODE best?

explanation.en: GPL lets anyone use, modify and redistribute software, provided derived versions are also released under GPL (copyleft).

passage.en: A college music club records an original song and wants others to share it freely, but only with credit to the club and not for commercial use. The club's app developer also writes code for the club website and wants anyone to be able to use, modify and redistribute the code, as long as their changes are also shared under the same terms.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Copyright protects the expression of an idea, such as the text of a book or the code of a program.
Reason (R): An idea itself can be copyrighted even if it is not expressed in any form.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is true. R is false: copyright protects the expression, not the bare idea.

stem.en: Fake emails or websites that trick users into revealing passwords, bank or card details are called:

explanation.en: Phishing uses fraudulent messages that look genuine to steal sensitive information.

stem.en: Malware that encrypts or locks a user's files and demands money to unlock them is:

explanation.en: Ransomware holds data "to ransom" and demands payment for access.

stem.en: A hacker who is authorised by an organisation to find and fix weaknesses in its system is called:

explanation.en: Ethical or white hat hackers work with permission to improve security; black hat hackers break in illegally.

stem.en: Secretly intercepting a private conversation or data travelling over a network is:

explanation.en: Eavesdropping is the unauthorised real-time interception of private communication.

solution.en: Eavesdropping is the unauthorised real-time interception of private communication.

stem.en: Which practice does NOT help in preventing cyber crime?

options.en: Clicking a "You won ₹10 lakh!" link to check if it is real
Keeping the operating system and antivirus updated
Logging out of accounts on shared computers
Using strong, different passwords with two-factor authentication

explanation.en: Opening links in unsolicited prize messages is a common phishing trap. The other three are standard safety measures.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Cyber bullying includes posting rude, threatening or embarrassing content about someone online.
Reason (R): Cyber bullying can harm a victim only when it is done by a stranger.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is true. R is false: bullying by classmates or known people is equally harmful — and often more common.

stem.en: The Indian Information Technology Act was passed in ____ and amended in ____.

explanation.en: The IT Act, 2000 was amended in 2008.

stem.en: Which of these is provided by the IT Act, 2000?

options.en: Legal recognition of electronic records and digital signatures

explanation.en: The Act gives legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures and deals with cyber crimes and penalties.

solution.en: The Act gives legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures and deals with cyber crimes and penalties.

stem.en: The study of designing furniture and devices so that they fit the user and reduce strain on the body is called:

explanation.en: Ergonomics designs workplaces and devices for comfort and safety of the user.

stem.en: A student uses his phone for 9 hours a day, feels restless when it is away and his marks have dropped. This is most likely a sign of:

explanation.en: Compulsive, excessive use that affects daily life and studies indicates Internet (or device) addiction.

stem.en: Which practice does NOT reduce the health impact of long computer use?

options.en: Taking regular short breaks and blinking often
Sitting with the back straight and feet flat on the floor
Keeping the top of the monitor at or slightly below eye level
Keeping the screen very close to the eyes in a dark room

explanation.en: A screen too close in a dark room increases eye strain. The other three are recommended ergonomic habits.

stem.en: Which change will MOST directly reduce her neck pain?

options.en: Using a table and chair with the screen near eye level
Switching to a smaller phone screen

explanation.en: Proper ergonomics — screen at eye level, back supported — prevents bending the neck.

passage.en: Priya, a 1st PUC student, studies online for 3 hours and then plays games on her laptop for another 4 hours every day. She sits on her bed with the laptop on her lap, bending her neck. Lately she complains of neck pain, dry eyes and poor sleep, and she gets irritated when asked to stop gaming.

stem.en: Her irritation when asked to stop gaming and her poor sleep most likely indicate:

explanation.en: Irritability when stopped and disturbed sleep are typical signs of addiction to devices or gaming.

stem.en: Which of the following is an example of a passive digital footprint?

options.en: A comment you post on a blog
Cookies recording the websites you visit
An e-mail you send to a friend
An online admission form you fill in

explanation.en: A passive footprint is collected without your direct action, as cookies do. Posting, e-mailing and filling forms are things you do on purpose, so they are active footprints.

solution.en: A passive footprint is collected without your direct action, as cookies do.
Posting, e-mailing and filling forms are things you do on purpose, so they are active footprints.

stem.en:
Match the intellectual property right with what it protects.
(A) Copyright  (B) Patent  (C) Trademark
(i) The logo of a company
(ii) The code of a software program or a novel
(iii) A new invention

explanation.en: Copyright protects creative and literary expression such as code and books; a patent protects an invention; a trademark protects a brand name or logo.

solution.en: Copyright protects creative and literary expression such as code and books; a patent protects an invention; a trademark protects a brand name or logo.

stem.en: Ravi gets an e-mail that looks like it is from his bank. It asks him to click a link and type his password to “verify” his account. This is an example of:

explanation.en: Phishing uses fake e-mails and websites that imitate a trusted organisation to trick people into giving their passwords or other details.
